mechanism_narrative: Rising GDP indicates strong economic activity, which should positively impact S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: If GDP growth is positive but S&P 500 returns are negative more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in unemployment rate suggests a strong labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If unemployment drops below 4% but S&P 500 returns are negative more than 35% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: When both unemployment rate decreases and employment increases, it indicates a strong economy, leading to positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If both proxies improve but S&P 500 returns are negative more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: High federal funds rate during a tightening cycle may lead to negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.5% but S&P 500 returns are positive more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: Increasing industrial production suggests strong economic output, leading to positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If industrial production grows but S&P 500 returns are negative more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: Rising housing starts indicate increased demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over 60 days.
failure_condition: If housing starts exceed 1200 but S&P 500 returns are negative more than 35% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: When both retail sales and housing starts increase, it signals strong demand, leading to positive S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If both proxies increase but S&P 500 returns are negative more than 40% of the time.

mechanism_narrative: In a tightening cycle, high federal funds rate and low unemployment may lead to negative S&P 500 returns.
failure_condition: If both conditions are met but S&P 500 returns are positive more than 35% of the time.
